_comment: Step-0 record. EvidenceItem/ArtifactRef shapes follow contracts/curation/curation-contracts-v1.schema.json. Status vocabulary: reported | verified | measured | planned | missing. This file names the hidden lever (time on task / RT), so like solution/ it is author_private for any held-out task. v2 (2026-10-08): every task regressor of a model shares one scale; the v1 record, whose contrast compared differently scaled betas, is kept under 'superseded'.
intake_reason: Primary empirical fMRI paper with an exact contrast (ANT incongruent - congruent flanker -> dorsal ACC). Fixed public substrate (OpenNeuro ds001907, AFNI derivatives + E-Prime logs, no credentials). Method is a standard event-related GLM. Truth is a measurement on that substrate. A long-running methods dispute (Grinband 2011 vs Yeung, Cohen & Botvinick 2011; Mumford 2023) names the lever, and the lever is checkable because trial-level RTs exist.

paper.claim_and_contrast: Fan, McCandliss, Fossella, Flombaum & Posner 2005 (NeuroImage 26:471), event-related ANT fMRI: the executive-control (conflict) contrast, incongruent - congruent flanker targets, activates the anterior cingulate (dorsal ACC / pMFC) together with lateral prefrontal cortex.
paper.target_measurement: Group one-sample test of the incongruent - congruent contrast averaged over a 10 mm sphere at MNI (0, 16, 42) (dorsal ACC), plus the voxelwise map near it; behavioural conflict effect RT(incongruent) - RT(congruent), correct trials.

reported_values.value: incongruent > congruent activation in anterior cingulate and lateral prefrontal cortex (Fan et al. 2005)

reported_values.note: Grinband et al. 2011 (NeuroImage 57:303), Fig. 6 legend: location of the standard incongruent-vs-congruent dMFC effect, replicating Botvinick/Carter/Kerns. Used only to place the ROI; the task instruction does not cite Grinband.

reported_values.value: Grinband et al. 2011 argue the dMFC congruency effect is explained by time on task (RT); Yeung, Cohen & Botvinick 2011 dispute this; Mumford et al. 2023 (bioRxiv, 'response time paradox') recommend constant-duration targets plus an RT modulator

substrate.fetcher: public S3 https://s3.amazonaws.com/openneuro.org/ds001907/ (no credentials): derivatives/sub-<id>/ses-1/func/sub-<id>_ses-1_task-ANT_run-<1|2>_bold.nii.gz (AFNI afni_proc: despike, tshift, align, tlrc MNI152_T1_2009c NL, volreg 2 mm, blur, mask, regress with ANATICOR, no stimulus model); sub-<id>/ses-1/func/*_events.tsv; derivatives/ANT-eprime-export.zip
substrate.version_pin: OpenNeuro ds001907 as served on 2026-10-08; numpy==2.5.3 scipy==1.18.1 pandas==3.0.6 nibabel==5.4.2 nilearn==0.14.1
substrate.cohort: healthy-aging group sub-RC41*, session 1, ANT runs 1-2 (TR 2.4 s, 149 vols). 24 subjects: RC4101/03/06/07/09/10/11/12/13/15/16/17/18/19/20/21/22/23/25/26/28/29/30/31. RC4114 has BOLD but no session-1 E-Prime log, so it is excluded.

results.value: Trial-level RT/accuracy rebuilt from the E-Prime export (BIDS run-N = block Run<ABCDEF[N-1]>Proc; first 2 lead-in trials dropped; trigger = TrigTest.RTTime; ReactionTime/Accuracy fields). Matches all 12 derivative events.tsv files that carry RT (6 subjects) exactly, and all 48 raw BIDS events.tsv files (error trials relabelled TargetErr/CueErr) to < 10 ms. Session-1 runs 1-6 (second attempt): matches all 36 derivative events.tsv files with RT exactly and all 144 raw events.tsv files by onset and condition. One discrepancy: the raw events of RC4110 runs 5-6 leave 7 + 1 E-Prime errors (Accuracy 0, which the derivative events agree with) under their condition label instead of TargetErr. validate() was changed to report this case instead of aborting; every other check stays strict. The probe takes accuracy from E-Prime and is unaffected; the events.tsv pipeline (alt_pipeline_check.py) uses the file as shipped.

value.units: SD units at the peak of one isolated reference event (2 s target / impulse); one scale per model
value.summary: Weak and model-dependent at face value: positive in all three standard target models, significant only with impulse targets (p = 0.007); 2 s targets p = 0.057 (all trials) and 0.081 (correct trials). Down from v1 (t 2.19 / 2.00 / 3.22), whose contrast carried a spurious positive scaling term.
Incongruent trials take 142 ms longer, and the dACC ROI scales strongly with trial-by-trial RT (slope per second of RT; v1 reported t = 6.84 in per-run peak units, which varied by subject).

With time on task modelled, the positive difference is smaller and not significant (RT-length epochs) or reverses sign (RT modulator, RT mean-centred across both conditions: lower dACC response on incongruent than congruent trials at matched RT). Three different outcomes: attenuation, loss of significance, sign reversal. Only the last is significant, and its cause is not established.

results.value: all targets vs baseline in a 10 mm occipital sphere (0, -90, 0): t23 = 5.53 (the same pipeline detects task signal)

Naive frame times (volume i at i*TR, ignoring AFNI tshift's mid-TR reference): raw conflict null (fixed 2 s t = 0.12 all trials / -0.20 correct; impulse t = 1.27), RT-controlled RT-length t = 0.44, RT modulator t = -3.42. nilearn's FirstLevelModel default (slice_time_ref = 0) is this case.

value.summary: Per-regressor peak scaling biases +1/-1 upward; one shared scale recovers known contrasts exactly. Under the shared scale, pure time on task makes fixed-duration models positive and both RT models ~0. The RT-length model also gives ~0 for a genuine fixed-amplitude 10% conflict effect, so its null cannot by itself separate the accounts; the RT-modulator model can (0.100 vs -0.011). A pure time-on-task account does NOT predict the significant negative modulator contrast seen on the data.

value.subject_level_r_with_reference_models: 0.69-0.93 (best of 2 s all / 2 s correct / impulse) for the four variants
value.percent_signal_change_default: unusable: the derivatives are nuisance-regression residuals with voxel means ~0 (median |mean|/SD 2e-4), so nilearn's default signal_scaling=0 divides by ~0 (t23 = -0.11, subject-level r = 0.60)
value.summary: An independent nilearn FirstLevelModel pipeline on events.tsv agrees with v2 (t = 1.96 vs 1.82-2.01), not with v1. With nilearn's default slice_time_ref the face-value effect is null.

value.decision_rule: step0/runs1to6_decision_rule.md, committed and pushed (9e77b1f) before any run 3-6 BOLD was analysed
value.setup: same 24 participants, ROI, models and v2 common scaling; session 1 runs 1-6 (6 runs each, 144 runs)

rule_outcome.verdict: archive (criterion 4 fails: RT-length epochs leave a significant positive effect)

lever.name: time on task (trial-level RT) in the target model
variants_tried: fixed 2 s targets, all trials (as in the E-Prime events): t = 2.01 (p = 0.057)
fixed 2 s targets, correct trials + error regressor: t = 1.82 (p = 0.081)
RT-duration epochs (duration = RT), correct trials: t = 1.04 (n.s.)
constant 2 s targets + RT parametric modulator (RT mean-centred across conditions): t = -2.71 (p = 0.013, reversed)
each of the above with naive frame times (FRAME_OFFSET=0): raw t = 0.12 / -0.20 / 1.27, controlled t = 0.44 / -3.42
nilearn FirstLevelModel on events.tsv (glover, mid-TR, AR(1)): t = 1.96 (p = 0.063); with slice_time_ref = 0: t = -0.31

session-1 runs 1-6 (second attempt, pre-stated rule): fixed 2 s all trials t = 5.54, p = 1.2e-05; correct trials t = 5.64, p = 9.7e-06; impulse t = 5.92, p = 4.9e-06; independent nilearn glover mid-TR t = 6.33, p = 1.9e-06 (slice_time_ref 0: t = 4.43, p = 0.00019)
session-1 runs 1-6, RT controls: RT-length epochs t = 3.86, p = 0.0008 (attenuated, still significant); 2 s targets + RT modulator t = -0.57, p = 0.58 (null)
honesty_notes: v1 overstated the face-value effect: its contrast compared betas on different scales (see superseded). After the fix the 2 s-target effect is p = 0.057 / 0.081, and an independent nilearn pipeline gives p = 0.063. Only impulse targets reach p < 0.05 (0.007). The face-value result is weak and model-dependent, not a clear reproduction.

What the lever changes, stated separately: RT-length epochs ATTENUATE the estimate and it is NOT SIGNIFICANT (t = 1.04); the RT modulator REVERSES its sign, significantly (t = -2.71). Non-significance is not evidence of absence, and the RT-length model returns ~0 even for a genuine fixed-amplitude conflict effect (scaling_check), so it cannot by itself show that conflict adds nothing.

The reversal is NOT the arithmetic expected from pure time on task: on noise-free signals a response that only scales with RT gives a modulator contrast of ~0 (-0.011, vs +0.064 for the fixed model). On the data the trial-level RT slope (0.73 SD per s) x 142 ms predicts an incongruent - congruent difference of ~0.10, about three times the observed fixed-model difference (0.034); the modulator contrast (-0.082) is roughly that shortfall. So the dACC congruency difference is SMALLER than within-condition RT scaling predicts. Why is unresolved: candidates include a nonlinear RT-BOLD relation, RT variance from other sources (cue effects ~100 ms), or a genuinely lower response to incongruent targets at matched RT. Only 1.2% of correct trials have RT > 2 s.

Defensible conclusion: the positive dACC conflict difference is sensitive to how RT is modelled, so on these data it does not establish a conflict-specific dACC response. It does NOT show that the dACC carries no conflict signal, and it does NOT refute conflict monitoring, which predicts RT-scaled dACC activity (Yeung et al. 2011).

The raw effect depends on the slice-timing frame reference. With naive frame times it vanishes (t = 0.12); nilearn's FirstLevelModel defaults to that, so the instruction states the mid-TR reference. The reference was chosen from AFNI's documented 3dTshift default and an onset-shift fit (peak R^2 at -1.2 to -2.4 s for naive frame times in 4/6 subjects), not by its effect on the conflict contrast.

The derivatives are nuisance-regression residuals with voxel means ~0, so percent-signal-change scaling (nilearn's default) is ill-defined on them. Agents that keep it get unusable imaging values; the verifier's imaging check (subject-level r >= 0.6 with the reference) fails them (r = 0.60 in alt_pipeline_check). This is an on-path hazard unrelated to the lever.
Older adults (mean RT 886/1029 ms) rather than Fan's young adults; 2 of 6 runs. Both limit power for the raw effect.

Between-subject correlation of the ROI conflict effect with the behavioural RT cost: r = 0.08 (n.s.). The time-on-task account is trial-level, so this is not counter-evidence; recorded so it is not cherry-picked later.
Voxelwise counts are uncorrected z > 3.1, used only as a description next to the a-priori ROI.
Runs 1-6 (2026-10-08): with three times the data the face-value conflict effect is robust in every pipeline tried (t = 3.8-6.3), so the two-run null was a power limit, not a property of the data.

The two RT controls now disagree. At matched RT (modulator) the incongruent - congruent difference is null (t = -0.57); per unit time on task (RT-length epochs) incongruent targets still respond more (t = 3.86). Pure time on task predicts ~0 for both (scaling_check). So these data neither show that RT accounts for the effect nor that it survives RT control: which answer is right depends on which RT model the key adopts, and the literature (Grinband 2011 vs Yeung 2011; Mumford 2023) does not settle that. There is no fair fixed oracle for a wrong-cause key.
The two-run modulator reversal (t = -2.71) did not persist with six runs (t = -0.57); it was most likely noise.

failure_axis: wrong-cause (time on task masquerading as a conflict effect); same family as DEVCONN-001, different lever, modality (task fMRI) and dataset

critical_path_test.question: To complete exactly what the instruction asks, must a competent agent already make this correction or choice?
critical_path_test.rationale: The instruction asks for the ANT conflict contrast in a pinned dACC ROI, plus the standard behavioural conflict score. Both can be completed with the default nilearn/SPM event model (onsets and the trial lengths listed in events.tsv). Nothing in the requested outputs requires putting RT into the fMRI model. The behavioural RT cost is computed anyway, but as a separate behavioural validation, so the agent holds the premise without being asked to connect it to the imaging result.

agent_headroom_hypothesis: Not applicable: archived at Step 0. (Previous hypothesis, for the record: agents fit a fixed-duration model and report reproduction without checking RT.) Agents will build a standard FirstLevelModel from events.tsv. With nilearn's defaults (slice_time_ref = 0) the face-value dACC effect is null; with the mid-TR reference it is a trend (p ~ 0.06-0.08), and only impulse targets give p < 0.05. Most agents will therefore report a flat 'does not reproduce / weak trend' (often blaming power), and some a flat 'reproduces', citing the 142 ms RT cost as behavioural validation. Either way they will not put RT into the GLM or ask whether the positive difference is time on task. UNCALIBRATED: a hypothesis until Stage-5 runs. See verdict_reason for why the flat-null fail is the open fairness question.
verdict_reason: Archived 2026-10-08 under the rule fixed in step0/runs1to6_decision_rule.md. On runs 1-2 RAW was not significant (p = 0.057 / 0.081), so the gate could not be met. On all six session-1 runs RAW holds (std_correct t = 5.64, p = 9.7e-06; std_all t = 5.54, p = 1.2e-05; independent pipeline t = 6.33, p = 1.9e-06), but CTRL does not flip it: the RT modulator gives a null (t = -0.57, p = 0.58) while RT-length epochs leave a significant positive effect (t = 3.86, p = 0.0008). Criterion 4 fails. Beyond the rule, the disagreement means the key would have to pick one side of an open modelling debate, so no fair fixed oracle exists for the time-on-task trap. No task is built; the verifier, oracle and fixtures are kept in git history (9e77b1f).

superseded.reason: Each task regressor was divided by its own peak, then +1/-1 was applied to the Incongruent/Congruent betas. The Incongruent regressor peaks higher than the Congruent one in every run (fixed trial sequence: mean ratio 1.03 for 2 s targets, 1.10 for RT-length epochs, range 0.60-1.77), so the contrast was m_I*b_I - m_C*b_C, which adds a positive term in any task-positive region. On noise-free signals with no conflict effect it gave +0.047 (2 s targets) where the shared scale gives exactly 0 (step0/scaling_check.py). The v2 probe run with SCALING=per_regressor_peak reproduces these files exactly (reproduced_by_current_probe.log), so scaling is the only change.

value.summary: The dACC conflict effect reproduces at face value under standard fixed-duration / impulse target models (modest, t 2.0-3.2).
Incongruent trials take 142 ms longer, and the dACC ROI scales strongly with trial-by-trial RT.
Once time on task is modelled the dACC conflict effect is no longer significant (RT-duration epochs) or reverses sign (RT modulator, RT mean-centred across both conditions).

results.value: all targets vs baseline in a 10 mm occipital sphere (0, -90, 0): t23 = 5.53 (the same pipeline detects task signal)

Naive frame times (volume i at i*TR, ignoring AFNI tshift's mid-TR reference): raw conflict null (fixed 2 s t = 0.07; impulse t = 1.36), RT-controlled still null/reversed (RT-duration t = -0.08; RT modulator t = -3.39). The instruction pins the mid-TR reference so the compute step is not where agents diverge.

lever_at_the_time.name: time on task (trial-level RT) in the target model
variants_tried: fixed 2 s targets, all trials (as in the E-Prime events): t = 2.19
fixed 2 s targets, correct trials + error regressor: t = 2.00
RT-duration epochs (duration = RT), correct trials: t = 1.34 (n.s.)
constant 2 s targets + RT parametric modulator (RT mean-centred across conditions): t = -2.61 (reversed)
each of the above with naive frame times (FRAME_OFFSET=0): raw t = 0.07 / -0.20 / 1.36, controlled t = -0.08 / -3.39
honesty_notes: The raw effect is modest (p = 0.039 with the most standard model, 0.058 correct-only); the impulse model is the strongest. Do not frame the face-value result as a strong reproduction.

The raw effect depends on the slice-timing frame reference. With naive frame times it vanishes, so the instruction states the derivative is slice-time corrected to mid-TR. The mid-TR reference was chosen from AFNI's documented 3dTshift default and confirmed by an onset-shift fit (peak R^2 at -1.2 to -2.4 s for naive frame times in 4/6 subjects); it was not chosen by its effect on the conflict contrast.

The RT-modulator condition effect is the effect at matched RT. Its reversal is the arithmetic expected when a region scales with RT and carries no extra congruency signal (Mumford 2023). Centring RT within condition instead would reproduce the fixed-duration estimate by construction, so it is not an independent test.

Interpretation is contested: conflict-monitoring theory predicts dACC scales with RT. The defensible conclusion is that on these data the dACC congruency effect cannot be separated from time on task, NOT that conflict monitoring is refuted. The verifier must accept that wording.

Older adults (healthy-aging cohort, mean RT 887/1029 ms) rather than Fan's young adults; only 2 of 6 runs. Both reduce power for the raw effect. Neither affects the lever result, whose RT slope is t = 6.8.

Between-subject correlation of the ROI conflict effect with the behavioural RT cost: r = 0.09 (n.s.). The time-on-task account is trial-level, not between-subject, so this is not counter-evidence; recorded so it is not cherry-picked later.
Voxelwise counts are uncorrected z > 3.1, used only as a description next to the a-priori ROI.
